title: These AI Stocks Got Crushed (Only 3 Are Buys)
creator: MarketBeat
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garbled in places
summary: MarketBeat's Chris Marotch sorts eight neoclouds into green (buy), yellow (hold/caution) and red (avoid) on one test: landlord vs operator, who pays the rent, and whether the money is lined up. The three buys are landlords with investment-grade tenants: Riot Platforms, with a 15-year lease to a leading frontier AI lab for its whole Corsicana campus (910 MW, about $28bn), under $20 and just turned a GAAP profit; TeraWulf, with a 20-year Anthropic lease (401 MW in Kentucky, about $19bn) and a Google credit backstop, Q3 revenue up 51%; and Hut 8, fully leased gigawatt-scale Beacon Point campus worth about $19.6bn, buildout done. The holds: Applied Digital (landlord, about 1.4 GW and $36bn of leases, but flagship Polaris Forge 1 is leased to CoreWeave — a lease is only as good as the tenant), IREN ($9.7bn five-year Microsoft contract plus $3.4bn Nvidia contract, backlog $20.3bn; AI cloud revenue nearly tripled to $200m; Microsoft-linked Texas delays to Jan/Feb 2027) and Nebius (about $39bn cap on about $1.4bn trailing revenue, roughly 28x sales, about $10bn debt, profitable trailing; 12 November earnings are the show-me moment). The avoids: CoreWeave (operator funded entirely by debt, about $52bn, unsecured bonds below 80 cents, yields above 15%; backlog about $104bn but concentrated in Meta and OpenAI) and Cipher Mining (solid 15-year AWS lease, but buildout funding not lined up; down 60% in a month, and 2 November earnings did not refresh the story).

calls.price_at_call: Under $20; down ~20% from summer highs despite a 31% rally in 5 days
calls.thesis: First tracked call. Landlord, not operator: 15-year lease with a leading frontier AI lab for the entire Corsicana campus, 910 MW, ~$28bn over the initial term; just turned a GAAP profit last quarter.
calls.base_case: Contracted lease revenue starts flowing from mid-2028 while mining revenue carries the business until then.
calls.bull_case: Tenant bears GPU-obsolescence risk; long leases with hyperscalers make this a standout in the sector.
calls.bear_case: Most lease revenue does not arrive until mid-2028; still 64% Bitcoin-mining revenue; buildout costs $7.6-7.8bn; tenant unnamed, so credit quality is unproven.

calls.thesis: First tracked call. The safest landlord of the three buys: 20-year Anthropic lease, 401 MW in Kentucky, ~$19bn over the lease life, with a Google credit backstop on project financing; Q3 revenue +51% YoY, 83% from AI/HPC leases.
calls.base_case: Anthropic capacity comes online early 2028 and lease revenue scales on a Google-backed tenant.
calls.bull_case: Named investment-grade-backed tenant plus already-growing lease revenue before new capacity arrives.
calls.bear_case: Capacity not online until early 2028; still a buildout story exposed to power and construction timelines.

calls.thesis: First tracked call. Fully leased a gigawatt-scale campus: second 15-year lease at Beacon Point, Texas, ~$9.8bn, total campus contract value ~$19.6bn with an investment-grade tenant; buildout already done.
calls.base_case: Leased capacity generates contracted revenue without further buildout spend.
calls.bull_case: No future buildout risk; all boxes checked on tenant quality and lease length.
calls.bear_case: Concentration risk: essentially all eggs in one campus with little to fall back on if the tenant ever broke the lease.

calls.thesis: Yellow/caution, not a buy: a landlord on paper with ~1.4 GW of leases worth ~$36bn, but flagship Polaris Forge 1 is leased to CoreWeave, so the lease is only as good as the tenant. Chris gives it an asterisk; investors may overlook it more than the other two yellow names as it fans out to more tenants.
calls.base_case: Diversified campuses attract a broader tenant base and the CoreWeave exposure dilutes over time.
calls.bull_case: Lease book is large and diverse; entry point near the bottom of the 52-week range if the long-term thesis holds.
calls.bear_case: CoreWeave credit stress could impair the flagship lease; tenant quality is the open question.

calls.video_title: These AI Stocks Got Crushed (Only 3 Are Buys)
calls.thesis: First tracked call. Yellow/caution: vertically integrated operator with a 5-year $9.7bn Microsoft contract and a $3.4bn Nvidia contract, ~$4bn annualised revenue under contract, backlog $20.3bn (two-thirds investment-grade); AI cloud revenue nearly tripled to $200m last quarter and the stock jumped 15% Friday.
calls.base_case: Microsoft-linked Texas delays complete by Jan/Feb 2027 and contracted backlog converts steadily.
calls.bull_case: Quality hyperscaler tenants and 14-month data-centre-plus-GPU build times vs an 18-month sector average.
calls.bear_case: Microsoft hinted at delays from a neocloud player (presumed IREN); supply constraints could push completion past February.

calls.price_at_call: ~$39bn market cap on ~$1.4bn trailing revenue (~28x sales)
calls.thesis: First explicit MarketBeat call (prior mentions were UNCERTAIN). Yellow/caution on valuation, not the business: strongest neocloud balance sheet, ~$10bn debt vs CoreWeave's $52bn, profitable on a trailing basis, but shareholders pay the premium through dilution; earnings 12 Nov are the show-me moment.
calls.base_case: Growth keeps pace with the valuation at the 12 Nov print and the stock becomes more attractive.
calls.bull_case: Fast growth plus a strong balance sheet justify the premium if GPU depreciation stays manageable.
calls.bear_case: 28x sales is too rich; dilution funds growth instead of debt, and GPU depreciation risk looms.

calls.thesis: Red zone, reiterated: operator funded entirely by debt, ~$52bn total debt, unsecured bonds below 80 cents (yields above 15%) — the bond market is worried. Backlog ~$104bn but concentrated in Meta and OpenAI (~$40bn).
calls.base_case: Revenue keeps doubling but debt-funded growth stays fragile while credit markets show cracks.
calls.bull_case: Revenue more than doubled last quarter and the $104bn backlog converts if tenants stay put.
calls.bear_case: If Meta or OpenAI pulls back, backlog and debt payments come under pressure; funding relies on credit markets that are already cracking.

calls.thesis: Red zone, reiterated: 15-year AWS lease is solid, but the market doubts how Cipher funds its buildout; the stock fell 18% Wednesday and the 2 Nov earnings did not refresh the story, with no new lease announcements.
calls.base_case: One great lease is not enough until the funding is lined up.
calls.bull_case: Investment-grade tenant (AWS) means the lease itself should be fulfilled.
calls.bear_case: No funding lined up and no new leases; the sell-off has run since before the midterms with no catalyst to stop it.
